book.name: Oxyrhynchus 1224
book.title: P.Oxy. X 1224 · Theological Fragments from an Uncanonical Gospel
book.translator: B. P. Grenfell and A. S. Hunt (1914)
book.sourceNote: The editors' English translations of the intelligible portions of Fragment 2 in The Oxyrhynchus Papyri, Part X (1914), no. 1224, printed pages 1–10. Brackets retain an editorial restoration; ellipses mark losses.
book.identityNote: Fragments from an unidentified gospel or gospel-like collection. Their physical order is uncertain. Fragment 1 preserves too little for the editors to translate and is recorded here as a completeness limitation rather than silently reconstructed.
book.rights: Grenfell and Hunt's 1914 English translation is public domain in the United States.

1.label: Fragment 2, recto column ii · numbered page 173
1.text: …overcame me. And Jesus stood by in a vision and said, Why art thou cast down? For it is not thou who… but he who gave (?)…

2.label: Fragment 2, verso column i · numbered page 174
2.text: …thou didst say…, making no answer. What then hast thou forbidden? What is the new doctrine that they say thou teachest, or what the new baptism that thou dost preach? Answer and…

3.label: Fragment 2, verso column ii · numbered page 175
3.text: The scribes and Pharisees and priests seeing him had indignation because he reclined in the midst of sinners. And Jesus hearing them said, They that are whole need not a physician, [but they that are sick].

4.label: Fragment 2, recto column i · numbered page 176
4.text: …and pray for your enemies; for he that is not against you is with you. He that to-day is afar off shall to-morrow be near you, and in… of the adversary…
